## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cūḷabyūha Sutta* (Snp 4.12, PTS Snp 171), also styled *Cūḷabyūhasutta* or *Cūlabyūha*, is a verse text belonging to the *Suttanipāta* [SuttaCentral]. Translated by Bhikkhu Sujato as "The Shorter Discourse on Arrayed For Battle", the sutta addresses how a spiritual practitioner should conduct themselves in a contentious world where rival teachers advance conflicting truths, questioning the multiplicity of dogmas when truth itself is singular [SuttaCentral]. In modern scholarship on early Buddhism, the sutta has been analyzed in debates regarding early Buddhist epistemological and mystical stances: researchers highlight its dismissal of dogmas, theories, and *saññā* (perception, verse 886), as well as its discussion of sectarians (*titthyā*, verses 891–892) and the figure of the *brāhmaṇa* who accomplishes the religious goal without adhering to canonical doctrines [Seyfort Ruegg and Schmithausen 1990].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral identify a counterpart in the Chinese Buddhist canon within the *Yizu jing* (T 198, 佛說義足經) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus additionally generates machine-based alignments with the Chinese *Qishi yinben jing* (T 25, 起世因本經), albeit with low similarity scores [DharmaNexus]. In Pali literature, the sutta forms the subject of an entire section of the canonical commentary, the *Cūḷabyūhasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 12) in the *Mahāniddesa* [SuttaCentral], with which DharmaNexus records extensive text reuse across 82 matching passages (over 7,700 characters, notably at segments §6.4–9.1) [DharmaNexus]. Further shared passages appear in the traditional commentaries, the *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Mahāniddesa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
